hearts.alpha_why: the owner, 2026-10-05: "for the pokemon species overhaul running, the boss pokemon are alphas, so it should sometimes be the pokemon in the area as well right?" Every heart entry (a heart is an area's boss table, section 10) compiles as a native Cobblemon 1.8.0 alpha: the spawn's PokemonProperties string carries alpha=true, the form the jar's own 1,082 spawn_pool_world/herds alpha leaders use (e.g. data/cobblemon/spawn_pool_world/herds/0023_fearow_alpha.json: "fearow held_item=cobblemon:flying_gem alpha=true"); alpha and is_alpha are PokemonProperties$Companion keys (Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar). tools/build_encounters.py stamps it on every generated heart entry and fails closed on a copied-through heart entry (marine band, waterway) without it.
hearts.alpha_level_matching: KEPT (the owner, 2026-10-05: "keep the alpha scaling"; nothing overlaid). NOT the authored band in game: the jar's behaviour data/cobblemon/behaviours/pokemon/auto/pokemon_non_party.json gives a wild alpha the sensor cobblemon:alpha_level_matching, which (AlphaLevelMatchingSensor$Companion.getTargetLevel) re-levels it, whenever a player is within 32 blocks and it is not battling, to that player's highest party level +4 (under 21), +8 (21-30), +12 (31-45), +16 (46-65) or +20, at most 100 and at least the level its species evolves at. The authored level is the level it spawns at; the level a player fights is the party's plus the step. Read from bytecode, not seen in game. Whether to keep this (it makes every boss above the party, so above every cap and past the next leg's) or overlay the behaviour without the sensor is the owner's decision.
hearts.local_alpha: every area's heart holds at least one species from its own base table (the owner's question above, 2026-10-05). Where a heart named none, it gains the strongest local stage: the highest base-stat total among the area's common and uncommon base species, mainline starters excluded (section 11), ties to the higher weight then the name; role uncommon at the presences' weight 3, so it stands beside them as one more boss

rules.corridor_rare_min_why: the owner, 2026-10-05: "every area should have a rare, ultra rare, and boss table"; the ruling the same day: a route corridor gets a rare and an ultra-rare table, reserved from the crossed on-path tables' rare- and ultra-role families (never an off-path find), but no heart (section 10: the path stays catchable)
rules.corridor_table_min_why: play test 2026-10-05 (review 85): a corridor box compiles only the route's listed species of its own table, and Pallet's meadows lost every slot but Caterpie to the route-wide ranking, so Route 1's first 180 blocks spawned Caterpie alone (113 route boxes held one or two species). Each crossed table keeps its three likeliest land species of the corridor roles before the rest is filled by score (measured over the 9 routes' boxes: one species at half or more of a box's weight in 163 boxes, from 330; none under three species; Pallet's stretch 12% Caterpie)
rules.corridor_species_ceiling_why: corridor_species_limit stops the fill by score; the species a route must keep (every crossed table's water species, the reserved rares, corridor_table_min per crossed table) may pass it, up to this ceiling, where the design fails closed

victory_road_roster.quote: some of the mons in victory road feel underwhelming, it should be hit after hit. why is vileplume there? why is breloom? crobat? i think its final starter evos and pseudo legendaries or bangers
victory_road_roster.by: the owner, 2026-10-06, after walking Victory Road
victory_road_roster.pools: every habitats pool whose id starts vrc_, and the _staple they carry
victory_road_roster.starter_families_source: base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobblemon/starters.json (the mainline starters; modpack/config/cobblemon/starters.json now lists the mythical ones), each walked to its family root in the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar
victory_road_roster.starter_finals_why: the owner, 2026-10-06: "thats to agressive on starters, technically most of those should be available in world somehow, we need variety": at most one starter final stage per Victory Road zone (the starter families also spawn wild elsewhere, ENCOUNTER_DESIGN.md section 11); the rest of each zone is non-starter bangers, none repeated across zones
victory_road_roster.why: Measured from the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar's species files (baseStats summed): the 27 mainline starters' final stages total 525-535, the pseudo-legendaries 600 (Baxcalibur is a client doll and stays out), so one predicate -- a final stage (no evolution in the jar) with a base-stat total of 500 or more, not legendary, mythical, an ultra beast or paradox -- admits all three of the owner's kinds: 186 species pass it once the client dolls are taken out, before the finds are. Crobat totals 535 and passes the number; the owner named it underwhelming, so it is out by name (owner_named_out), as are Vileplume (490) and Breloom (460), which the number already rejects. A find's family stays out (section 6: a find is never the base of a Victory Road family): Dragonite, Tyranitar, Salamence, Hydreigon and Kommo-o and the seven starter lines that are finds are an off-path table's reward and are not repeated here. tools/build_encounters.py fails closed on any vrc_ row that breaks this.

held_items.why: the owner, play test 2026-10-05: "wild held items, rare enough to be a find rather than a farm". A wild spawn of a listed species sometimes holds an item that fits it (a Leftovers Snorlax, a Lucky Egg Chansey); the chance is the main series' own 5% for a type booster or a stone, and 2% for an item a player would otherwise buy or earn (Leftovers, Lucky Egg, Light Ball, King's Rock, Quick Claw, Focus Band, Black Sludge, Ditto's powders), so a catch that comes with one is a find and catching a box of them to strip the items is not a plan
held_items.field_source: Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar: PokemonSpawnDetail has the field heldItems (List<PossibleHeldItem>); PossibleHeldItemAdapter reads an object {"item": <item id, or #tag>, "percentage": <number>}. PokemonSpawnDetail.createSpawnAction (javap -c, read 2026-10-05) takes the chance of no item as 1 - sum(percentage / 100), and when that roll does not come up picks one listed item weighted by its percentage, so a percentage is a chance out of 100 per spawn. None of the jar's own 1,544 spawn_pool_world files uses the field: VERIFIED from bytecode, NOT seen in game
held_items.where: every spawn_pool_world entry tools/build_encounters.py writes or copies through (sub-region rosters and their hearts, route corridors, the waterway, the marine bands) whose species is listed, stamped as held_items and written by tools/compile_spawns.py as heldItems. NOT habitat-block pools (a Habitat Block's pool spawn is a different format; no heldItems field was verified for it) and NOT the Mega field dens (tools/compile_spawns.py mega_den_spawns, from data/gulch_mine.json, not from data/spawns.json)
held_items.percent_why: the main series' wild held-item rates (50% common, 5% rare, 1% very rare; from memory, not a cited source) as the scale. Nothing here is common: 5% for a type booster, a stone or a bone; 2% for an item with a strong battle effect, between rare and very rare because a Cobblemon player meets far more wild spawns than a main-series one; at most max_total_percent per species, so 19 of 20 spawns of any species hold nothing
